help.intro: A warehouse is where stock is held and, just as importantly, the place an order ships from. That second job is why a business tracking no stock at all still needs one: a kitchen sending out food owns no inventory, but the order still left from somewhere.
help.step_1_body: The address is required and is picked from the addresses that already exist - search from three characters. It cannot be one that has been deleted, and it is refused rather than silently accepted, so create the address first if it is missing.
help.step_2_body: The code is the short name a warehouse is called by day to day, up to 16 characters. It is unique among warehouses that are not deleted, and a taken one is refused - so the code is the field worth agreeing on before anyone types it.
help.step_3_title: Decide whether it is the default
help.step_3_body: At most one warehouse is the default, and ticking it here takes the flag off whichever one held it before - there is no error to resolve, the previous default is simply no longer default. It exists so a single-site business never has to pick a warehouse at all.
help.step_4_body: A warehouse is active or inactive, and moves freely between the two. Status is a flag rather than a lock: nothing here stops an inactive warehouse being referenced, and deactivating the default one leaves it the default. Treat inactive as "no longer in use".
help.step_5_body: Search matches the name and the code from three characters, except for an all-digit term, which is treated as an id and matched exactly. Filter by status and by whether a warehouse is the default, and order by id, code or name.
help.note: Deleting a warehouse is a soft delete, and it releases both the code and the default flag - another warehouse can claim either while this one is gone. That is also why a restore can be refused: if the code was taken in the meantime, the row cannot come back until the conflict is resolved.
